Body.Content:
What and why

Use case classification is coming to public preview for Microsoft Frontier public tenants. This capability classifies agent sessions and user activity in Microsoft Copilot Cowork against a predefined taxonomy of use cases.

These insights help organizations understand the work performed by users and agents, identify which use cases consume the most AI credits, and find opportunities to consolidate agents and optimize AI investments. Use case classification also provides the foundation for AI value metrics, including AI value for Copilot Cowork.

Rollout schedule

  • Frontier preview: Beginning in mid-November 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Frontier public tenants using eligible agents or Microsoft Copilot Cowork

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Microsoft Copilot Cowork
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft Copilot Studio
  • Azure AI Foundry
  • Agent 365 Connected platforms

What will happen

Use case classification will be enabled by default for eligible Frontier tenants and users. AI value calculations, currently limited to Copilot Cowork user activity, will also be enabled by default.

The capability supports two types of activity:

Agent sessions

  • Sessions from agents built with Copilot Studio and Azure AI Foundry, declarative agents, and third-party agents registered through Agent 365 Connected platforms will be classified according to the work performed.
  • Eligible admins can review use cases and session counts in the agent Activity tab and Agent Map in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • These classifications are not shared with end users or agent makers.

Work activity in Microsoft Copilot Cowork

  • User activity in Copilot Cowork will be assigned to the predefined use case that most closely represents the work performed.
  • Eligible admins can view aggregated Cowork use cases, associated costs, and estimated value in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Cost Management > Consumption > Use cases.
  • Admins can disable classification for specific users or groups, and eligible users can opt out through the Data and privacy tab in their Microsoft profile editor.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required. Use case classification and AI value calculations will be enabled by default for eligible Frontier tenants and users.

Global Administrators and AI Administrators can manage these capabilities through three independent controls:

  • Agent session classification: Turn off classification for the entire tenant in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Agents > Settings > Activity classification.
  • Copilot Cowork work activity classification: Use Feature access management to create a policy that disables classification for the entire organization, specific groups, or individual users. Eligible users can also opt out through the Data and privacy tab in their Microsoft profile editor.
  • AI value calculations: Turn AI value metrics on or off and customize the inputs used to calculate AI value in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Agents > Settings > AI value. AI value calculations based on use case classifications are currently limited to Copilot Cowork.

We recommend that admins:

  • Review the available classification and AI value controls to determine whether changes are needed to align with organizational requirements.
  • Consider notifying users about work activity classification and the available opt-out option.

Additional considerations:

  • When classification is turned off, it stops within one day. Existing classification results are hidden, not deleted.
  • If classification is turned back on, it resumes from that point without classifying activity from the period when it was disabled.
  • Classifications use a predefined taxonomy rather than tenant-specific categories, so confidential project names are not surfaced as use cases.
  • Individual user classifications are not visible to other people. Organization leaders see work activity use cases only as aggregated insights.
  • Classifications are directionally accurate and intended to identify organizational trends, not audit individual interactions.

Learn more

  • Manage Task Inferencing in Microsoft Copilot | Microsoft Support
  • Understand business use cases for agents in Microsoft 365 admin center (Frontier) | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

This change introduces AI-based classification of agent sessions and Copilot Cowork activity, with associated reporting and administrative controls.

Organizations should review these capabilities and controls against their privacy and compliance requirements.
